title: Young stars in the open star cluster NGC 2547
caption: The open star cluster NGC 2547, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: NGC 2547 · constellation Vela · about 1500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Bright stars of the open cluster NGC 2547 are scattered across this image from ESO's La Silla Observatory. Far in the background, between them, many remote galaxies appear, some clearly spiral in shape.

NGC 2547 lies about 1500 light-years away in the direction of Vela, well inside our own galaxy. The galaxies behind it are separate systems far beyond the Milky Way, so the scene spans an enormous range of distances, from nearby stars to faraway galaxies.

An open cluster is a loose group of young stars born together from the same cloud of gas and dust. Their shared age and distance make such clusters useful for studying how stars develop. The image was taken with the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope's Wide Field Imager.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (27.68 x 29.72 arcminutes) and distance (1500 light years), the frame spans roughly 12 × 13 light-years. Its light set out about 1,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image from the Wide Field Imager combines B, V and R filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Long camera exposures gather far more light than the eye can, bringing out remote galaxies far too faint to see directly.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture combines exposures through B, V and R filters, all in visible light. Long exposures of a nearby cluster also reveal much fainter objects far beyond it, such as these background galaxies.
alt: Bright stars of an open cluster, with many faint, distant galaxies in the background, some of them spiral-shaped.
